campus_notes: Compiled 2026-11-28 from Colorado State University Housing & Dining Services (housing.colostate.edu): the hall pages, the 2026-2027 Hall Rates page (room types, air conditioning and general-assignment share per hall), the Bed Lofting page, the Mail page (building addresses) and the Aggie Village pages. For 2026-27 CSU runs eleven residence halls: Academic Village (Aspen, Honors and Engineering), Braiden, Corbett, Durward, Edwards, Ingersoll, Laurel Village (Alpine and Piñon), Newsom, Parmelee, Summit and Westfall; Allison Hall is closed for renovation and reopens Fall 2027, so it is left out. CSU's own undergraduate apartments, Aggie Village, are included; its Graduate & Family Apartments (Aggie Village Family, University Village, and International House, which is for undergraduates over 21 and graduate students) are left out. CSU publishes undimensioned floor plans and 3D tours for every hall room type but no room sizes, so every residence hall room uses the site's estimate fallback and is labelled 'Estimated based on similar rooms. Official size not published.' Economy doubles are smaller than CSU's other doubles, so their estimates run large. Aggie Village's renderings and the Lodgepole shared-bedroom drawings carry dimensions, recorded as published. Hall beds are extra-long twins (39" x 80") set at about 20 in and loftable; Aggie Village private bedrooms have full XL beds.

dorms.notes: CSU-run apartments opened 2016 for continuing undergraduates, transfer and graduate students (and new students over 21): Cottonwood (511 W. Lake St.), Lodgepole (521) and Walnut (501). Furnished, individual contracts, all utilities and Wi-Fi included, air conditioning, in-unit washer/dryer and dishwasher. Studio, one-, two-, three- and four-bedroom units; private bedrooms have a full XL bed, and Lodgepole's shared bedrooms two twin XL beds bunked.
